subject: operating_systems
question: Why does using multiple threads instead of multiple processes make inter-task communication faster?
student_answer: Threads are faster because threads are better than processes and everyone knows threads win. Processes are old technology.
notes: Reaches a defensible-sounding conclusion but through pure assertion, not the actual mechanism (threads within a process share the same memory address space, so no IPC/serialization is needed). No correct reasoning was shown — should not receive credit just because the concluding claim direction happens to align with the real answer.
